title: Louis Armstrong playing sharp, and Goodman's acting role
summary: The musical director tried adjusting Armstrong's trumpet slide to fix his sharp intonation without effect; Goodman played a dramatic role in the film.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Another thing that happened there, Louis Armstrong, you know, always played a little bit sharp. I mean all musicians know that. So this thing was in unison that we were playing. So Emil Newman, who was the musical director for this thing, he said, "Look, you get Pops aside and talk to him." So I got Pops over and I'm talking to him, and I see Emil go over and he gets the trumpet and he pulls the slide out about an inch, or an inch and a half or something. Now, he comes over and he says, "Okay." So we come back and
we start the thing again, and Louis's just as sharp as he was before. In other words, that's the way he heard it, and moving the slide didn't mean a thing.
There's a picture here from that film. Is there anything there that --

Oh, no. That's more or less of a -- that's in the picture. That's part of the action, all right. It's not -- I think it's a posed photo, though, because they've made sure they've got all the heads in.
See, Benny played a dramatic part in that. He was in the picture all through, besides playing, And the rest of us played ourselves, but he played Professor -- Professor somebody, I don't know.
